meta.what: Entry-by-entry comparison of the wiki dictionary (canon-lexicon.json) with the Dragon Language Dictionary, Fifth Edition, published by Thuum.org.
meta.fifth_edition_copy: Supplied by the project owner as a Word file on 2026-11-15 and kept in research/sources/thuum/; its parsed contents are in research/data/fifth-edition.json.
meta.kept_here: The comparison only: which words each source lists, the kind of official source the Fifth Edition cites for a definition, and likely spelling variants.

source_kinds.dialogue_file: developer notes in the game's dialogue file
source_kinds.prima_guide: the printed official guide, Legendary Edition
source_kinds.primagames_com: the guide publisher's online word list

meta.limits: The copy was a PDF converted to Word and holds 646 entries; its introduction says 647. One region was read by hand. Source kinds were read by pattern; an independent second parser agreed on all of them after correction, and about 75 entries were read in full. A few definitions are misprinted in the copy itself, so a cited source should be checked before it overrides another reading.

review_notes: Wiki "Quethsegol" is the first word of the Fifth Edition heading "Quethsegol Ahrol", where it is called a misspelling of qethsegol.
Wiki "Nall" and "Thurri" occur in the Fifth Edition only inside a quoted line marked [sic].
Fifth Edition "Daniik" has usage examples spelt daanik, which is the wiki headword.
Wiki "Vun" appears in the Fifth Edition only in a note under Zul.

Of the 59 wiki entries with no Fifth Edition heading, 21 cite only the untraced list, 17 cite The Elder Scrolls Online, 8 cite the book Wisdom of the Flying Gods, 1 cites Blades, 8 cite Skyrim sources, 3 the printed guide and 1 a Bethesda article.

Eight of those 59 occur in the Fifth Edition as inflected or compound forms in examples under another heading (Briinahii, Duaan, Frini, Funta, Junnesejer, Stinselok, Ziil, Zindro): it gives headings to base words only.
Seven of the 36 Fifth Edition headings missing from the wiki dictionary rows are on the same wiki page in other lists: six locations and one phrase.
Thaarn cites a book and the guide in its definition, but its usage note says it is attested only on the guide website; its level is doubtful.
Kun cites a dialogue line, but its entry says the word is inferred and the line reads jun; its level is doubtful.
